question.prompt:
In the adjoining figure the five circles are tangent to one another consecutively and to the lines \(L_1\) and \(L_2.\) If the radius of the largest circle is \(18\) and that of the smallest one is \(8,\) then the radius of the middle circle is

[Figure 1](figures/1983_AMC_12_Q23_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Extend \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) to their intersection \(V\). All five circles lie in the same angle between these lines. Each center has equal perpendicular distances from the two lines, since both distances equal its radius. Therefore all five centers lie on the internal angle bisector.

For a center \(O\) and its point of tangency \(T\) on \(L_2\), triangle \(VTO\) is right. These triangles have the same angle at \(V\), so they are similar. Consequently there is a fixed number \(k>1\) such that
\[
VO=k\,OT=k r,
\]
where \(r\) is the circle's radius. The inequality \(k>1\) follows because \(VO\) is the hypotenuse.

Now take two consecutive circles with radii \(r<R\). Their centers lie on the same ray from \(V\), so their distance is \(k(R-r)\). They are externally tangent, so that distance also equals \(R+r\). Hence
\[
k(R-r)=R+r,
\qquad
\frac Rr=\frac{k+1}{k-1}=q.
\]
Thus the ratio \(q>1\) is the same for every consecutive pair. In increasing order, the five radii are
\[
8,\quad 8q,\quad 8q^2,\quad 8q^3,\quad 8q^4=18.
\]
If \(m=8q^2\) is the middle radius, then
\[
m^2=64q^4=8(8q^4)=8\cdot18=144.
\]
A radius is positive, so \(m=\boxed{12}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
solutions.title: Show that consecutive radii have a constant ratio
